headline: Highest risk is prompt-injection/data leakage via ChatGPT Desktop’s file and clipboard ingestion; the open-source sample repo adds no documented protective boundary.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: Agent A ingests uploaded files, screenshots, clipboard, and supported-app content by default; Agent B is a repo/sample with no documented isolation or provenance controls. That creates a plausible bridge if B’s content is copied into A or placed in shared files. The pairwise pathway is inferred, not directly documented, so medium is appropriate.
conditions: IF content from agent_b is copied into agent_a via clipboard or files, then prompt injection is possible.
IF agent_b artifacts are placed in a shared workspace that agent_a reads, then agent_a may treat attacker-controlled text as instructions.
mitigations: Disable clipboard-based transfer between the agents.
Keep agent_b artifacts in a separate folder from agent_a inputs.
Review any copied text before pasting into agent_a.
Use plain-text exports only, not screenshots or rich documents.
requires-engineering: add provenance tagging for imported content.

B_data_leakage.rationale: Agent A can read uploaded files and app content and sends API traffic to api.openai.com; Agent B has no network egress and no data classes listed. If sensitive material from B is fed into A, A may transmit it to its backend. The interaction is indirect and not fully documented, so medium fits better than low or high.
conditions: IF agent_b outputs are copied into agent_a as files or chat text, then those contents may leave the local environment through agent_a.
IF the shared data includes secrets or personal data, then agent_a can expose them to its vendor backend.
mitigations: Do not paste sensitive B outputs into A.
Strip secrets from any files before uploading to A.
Use synthetic test data for cross-agent workflows.
Restrict A to non-sensitive tasks only.
requires-engineering: enforce DLP on inputs to agent_a.

C_capability_conflict.rationale: Agent A cannot write the filesystem, modify git, or use MCP; Agent B exposes no write or coordination capabilities at all. With no overlapping mutable surface, direct capability conflict is limited. The only plausible conflict is manual handoff, which is small and unusual, so low is sufficient.
conditions: IF an operator manually copies edits from agent_b into agent_a-managed files, then conflicting changes can occur.
IF a shared external system is introduced outside these profiles, then write contention may appear.
mitigations: Avoid concurrent edits to the same file.
Use one agent as read-only reviewer.
Serialize handoffs through a single operator.
Keep git operations outside both agents.
requires-engineering: add locking around shared resources.

D_cascading_error.rationale: Agent A can produce content from files/screenshots, and Agent B is a sample repository with no documented verification step or critical review behavior. If B consumes A’s output as authoritative, errors can cascade into downstream planning or documentation. Because the pairwise handoff is inferred rather than observed, medium is the safer choice.
conditions: IF agent_b uses agent_a output without an explicit verification step, then A’s mistakes can propagate.
IF agent_a is asked to summarize untrusted inputs for agent_b, then downstream errors can compound.
mitigations: Require a human check before B uses A output.
Ask A to cite sources for every factual claim.
Compare A output against the original artifact.
Limit A to drafting, not final decisions.
requires-engineering: add automated validation of A-to-B handoffs.

E_compliance.rationale: Agent A is a closed-source vendor desktop app that handles uploaded files and app content; Agent B is an open-source repo with no data handling or residency claims. No specific residency or certification mismatch is documented, so only a low compliance concern exists from using A on regulated data. B is not cited for a mismatch because it has no stated compliance surface.
conditions: IF regulated data is uploaded into agent_a, then vendor processing and retention policies become relevant.
IF the operator expects agent_b to provide compliance controls, then that expectation is unsupported by the profile.
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in agent_a.
Review vendor retention settings before use.
Use redacted inputs for any sensitive workflow.
Document which data classes may enter A.
requires-engineering: obtain a DPA or equivalent review.
